area: Audience need: Buying decisions and availability (Roman Urdu)
action: Add where-to-buy details, store link, warranty and PTA status to every video description and pinned comment, written in Roman Urdu.
evidence: 13.6% of substantive comments; present in 349 of 352 videos; 97% Roman Urdu.
limitation: Clusters overlap (silhouette 0.022) and K = 10 had a stability of 0.78 across random seeds.

area: Audience need: Device opinions and comparisons (English)
action: Offer English comparison summaries (a spec table in the description) for viewers who compare devices.
evidence: 11.8% of substantive comments; present in 347 of 352 videos; 18% Roman Urdu.
limitation: Clusters overlap (silhouette 0.022) and K = 10 had a stability of 0.78 across random seeds.

action: Use Buying guide videos when the goal is audience response, and treat Explainer videos mainly as information or reach content.
evidence: Like rate is 1.13x the channel's typical video for Buying guide (n = 85) versus 0.81x for Explainer (n = 23). Content types differ in like rate (p < 0.001), but not in views (p = 0.519).
limitation: Content type comes from title keywords, and channel style is only controlled by comparing each video with its own channel's typical video.

area: Audience need: Samsung and Motorola brand talk
action: Create head-to-head brand content (for example Samsung vs Motorola) and put brand names in titles, because viewers already discuss these brands.
evidence: 11.5% of substantive comments; present in 348 of 352 videos; 21% Roman Urdu.
limitation: Clusters overlap (silhouette 0.022) and K = 10 had a stability of 0.78 across random seeds.

area: Audience need: Gaming, performance and PTA requests (Roman Urdu)
action: Run a gaming-phone series with real FPS tests and a PTA / non-PTA checklist, and collect review requests in a pinned poll.
evidence: 11.2% of substantive comments; present in 343 of 352 videos; 90% Roman Urdu.
limitation: Clusters overlap (silhouette 0.022) and K = 10 had a stability of 0.78 across random seeds.

area: Audience need: Phone selection questions (Roman Urdu)
action: Publish budget-based 'which phone should I buy' guides (for example under 30k, 50k and 100k) in Roman Urdu, and answer selection questions with a link to the matching guide.
evidence: 10.8% of substantive comments; present in 341 of 352 videos; 95% Roman Urdu.
limitation: Clusters overlap (silhouette 0.022) and K = 10 had a stability of 0.78 across random seeds.

action: State the Pakistan price (PTA and non-PTA) in the first seconds of each video and keep a pinned price comment up to date.
evidence: 5.6% of substantive comments; present in 321 of 352 videos; 34% Roman Urdu.
limitation: Clusters overlap (silhouette 0.022) and K = 10 had a stability of 0.78 across random seeds.

action: Use Apple and Motorola content for reach, and add a clear call to action (a question or poll) because response per view is lower.
evidence: Apple: 1.40x views, 0.74x like rate, 0.66x comment rate (n = 26); Motorola: 1.40x views, 0.92x like rate, 1.06x comment rate (n = 17). Brands differ in views (p = 0.009).
limitation: Brand comes from the video title, and brand effects are mixed with content type and launch timing.

action: Plan launch-week content for Tecno and Oppo: unusual spikes cluster around these brands, so prepare unboxing, price and first-look videos before the launch.
evidence: Tecno: 5 of 17 videos (29%) flagged as unusual; Oppo: 5 of 25 videos (20%) flagged as unusual, versus 5% of all 352 videos.
limitation: Only 18 videos were flagged, and a spike may come from one launch event covered by several creators.

action: Measure audience demand only from customer-need comments; do not use total comment counts as a demand signal.
evidence: Only 53.8% of 29,561 clean comments express a customer need; 18.4% are praise or greetings, 11.3% are noise and 16.5% were flagged as chatter.
limitation: Cluster types were named by hand after reading cluster samples.

action: Write titles, pinned comments and replies in Roman Urdu, and keep English model names and keywords.
evidence: 62% of customer-need comments are Roman Urdu and 36% are English.
limitation: Language comes from a rule-based tag (92% accurate on 100 hand labels).
